question: What is the primary role of communication in nursing?

options.D: Passing time during long night shifts

explanation: Communication is the core tool nurses use to deliver safe, effective care and build relationships. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is effective communication especially important in busy clinical settings?

options.A: It bridges the gap between fear and understanding
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for written care plans
options.C: It reduces the total number of required nursing shifts
options.D: It prevents patients from asking too many questions

explanation: Clear interaction reassures patients and helps them feel secure despite busy hospital environments. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h1)

question: What component of the communication process confirms understanding by the receiver?
explanation: Feedback is the response that lets the sender know if the message was received and understood. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h2)

question: The medium used to transmit a message from the sender to the receiver is called what?
explanation: The channel is the pathway or medium, like spoken words or written text, used to carry the message. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which body posture signals genuine interest to a patient?

options.A: Looking away while writing in the chart
options.B: Sitting back with eyes closed to listen
options.C: Standing firmly with arms folded tightly
options.D: Uncrossed arms and leaning slightly forward

explanation: An open posture shows availability and encourages the patient to share more openly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h3)

question: A patient looks away uncomfortably when the nurse maintains direct eye contact. What should the nurse consider?

options.A: Direct eye contact is always mandatory in healthcare
options.B: Cultural norms regarding eye contact vary greatly
options.C: The patient is definitely hiding important health information
options.D: The patient has a severe visual impairment

explanation: Different cultures view direct eye contact differently; respecting these norms prevents patient discomfort. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of therapeutic communication?

options.D: Exclusively on the patient's health needs

explanation: Therapeutic communication centers entirely on the patient's well-being and clinical goals. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h4)

question: How does therapeutic communication differ from everyday social chat?

options.A: It avoids listening in favor of giving advice
options.C: It follows no professional guidelines whatsoever
options.D: It focuses equally on the nurse's personal life

explanation: Therapeutic communication is a purposeful nursing skill used to promote patient recovery and coping. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to effective communication?

options.A: Loud environmental noise on the ward

explanation: Using simple language actually enhances communication rather than blocking it. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why does severe pain or anxiety hinder a patient's communication?

options.A: It impairs their ability to process information
options.B: It prevents the nurse from writing in the chart
options.C: It forces them to speak only in medical terminology
options.D: It automatically cures their underlying medical condition

explanation: Overwhelming emotional or physical distress consumes mental energy, making concentration difficult. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the teach-back method?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to test the patient's memory
options.B: Replacing the need for written discharge forms
options.D: Confirming whether health instructions were understood

explanation: Teach-back requires patients to repeat information in their own words, verifying true comprehension. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h6)

question: A patient gives short 'yes' or 'no' answers during an assessment. What technique should the nurse use next?

options.A: Document that the patient refuses to speak at all
options.C: Ask open-ended questions to encourage elaboration
options.D: Repeat the same closed questions much louder

explanation: Open-ended questions prevent single-word replies and prompt the patient to share more detailed information. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is recommended when communicating with a patient who has dementia?

options.B: Giving one simple instruction at a time
options.C: Speaking rapidly to save valuable time

explanation: Short, single-step instructions prevent cognitive overload and reduce confusion in dementia patients. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h7)

question: An elderly patient struggles to hear questions during an admission interview. What should the nurse check first?

options.A: If the patient needs an emergency psychiatric evaluation
options.B: Whether the doctor prescribed the correct medication
options.C: Whether the patient's hearing aids are worn and working
options.D: If the patient is deliberately ignoring hospital staff

explanation: Checking for sensory assistive devices is a practical first step before assuming cognitive or language barriers. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h7)
